title: Train a world model in under 10 minutes for $0.1 of compute, and play it!
excerpt: A 14M-parameter world model of Craftax, a 2D Minecraft, learned from pixels and actions. Play it in your browser. Beat it in one 10-minute A100 run.
content_html:
GitHub

Every frame below is generated by a 14M-parameter world model on your GPU, one action at a time. Train your own, autoresearch style, and beat ours.

now playing: iteration 3 by Maharishiva

benchmark inside the model diamond speedrun checkpoints dataset github

autoresearch you can play

Point your coding agent at tinywmcraft: it trains a world model in 10 minutes, scores it, and tries again. Push the score up, then play the model you made: walk around inside it, craft, fight, and see what it gets wrong.

Beat 0.562 and yours is iteration 4: the crown goes next to your GitHub login, and the player on this page switches to your model. Paste this into your coding agent:

>/goal Clone https://github.com/Maharishiva/tinywmcraft, read program.md, get a GPU (a Google Colab A100 works: uv tool install google-colab-cli), beat the best world model under the rules on the three-seed mean, and only then open a pull request.

paste into Codex, Claude Code or any coding agent

The best so far, by the score: how close imagined play comes to the real game in looks, game logic and memory, and how well the model predicts rewards and deaths, from 0 for a trivial model to 1 for the real game.

  1. 1Maharishiva0.562 ± 0.017iteration 3 · train.py: shortcut loss, the heads' gradient into the trunk cut to a tenth in the second half, no hard-window mining, 1/8 game-start windows, two fused kernels, 349 lines
  2. 2Maharishiva0.463 ± 0.023iteration 2 · tile transformer tokenizer trained on clean, half-masked and noised frames, fused Pallas kernels, hard-window mining, half the windows from game starts, symlog two-hot reward head
  3. 3Maharishiva0.287 ± 0.019iteration 1 · train_tiny.py: the whole model in 178 lines, no custom kernels

crafting recipe book

wood pickaxe1 next to a table; mines stone and coal
wood sword1 next to a table
stone pickaxe1 1 next to a table; mines iron
stone sword1 1 next to a table
furnace1 on an open tile
iron pickaxe1 1 1 1 next to a table and a furnace; mines diamonds
iron sword1 1 1 1 next to a table and a furnace
place stone1 on grass, sand, path, water or lava

Wood comes from trees by hand, saplings from grass (1 hit in 10); stone and coal need a wood pickaxe, iron a stone pickaxe, diamonds an iron pickaxe. "Next to" is one of the 8 tiles around you. These are the real game's rules: the world model learned them from pixels and does not always keep them. In the real game, the first unlock of each of the 22 achievements is worth +1.

how it works

tinywmcraft is a world model of Craftax-Classic, a 2D Minecraft, learned from scratch from pixels and actions alone. Given a history of frames and an action, it generates the next frame, the reward and whether the episode ends; feed its own frames back in and you can play inside it. Every world in the player starts from a first frame the model imagines from noise: nothing is replayed. 13.9M parameters (5.2M tokenizer, 8.6M world model), trained cold in under 10 minutes on one A100, about $0.1 of compute.

Colab Pro: $9.99 for 100 compute units, and a 40 GB A100 uses about 5.4 an hour (~$0.55/h). A full submission, three seeds with their evals, is under $0.5.
